bootstrap

Bootstrap the sample mean

Stata 

bootstrap mean=r(mean), reps(199): summarize y

R boot 

boot::boot(data,statistic=function(d,i) mean(d$y[i]),R=199)

Fixed workflow. Random streams and resampling defaults differ across software; a fixed R seed makes this workflow reproducible.

6 more examples and alternatives

Bootstrap regression coefficients within fixed strata

Stata 

bootstrap _b, reps(199) strata(g): regress y x

R boot 

boot::boot(data,statistic=function(d,i) stats::coef(stats::lm(y~x,data=d[i,])),R=199,strata=data$g)

Fixed workflow. Random streams and resampling defaults differ across software; a fixed R seed makes this workflow reproducible.

Stata reference · R reference

Bootstrap a difference between regression slopes

Stata 

bootstrap difference=(_b[x]-_b[z]), reps(199): regress y x z

R boot 

boot::boot(data,statistic=function(d,i) unname(diff(stats::coef(stats::lm(y~x+z,data=d[i,]))[c("z","x")])),R=199)

Fixed workflow. Random streams and resampling defaults differ across software; a fixed R seed makes this workflow reproducible.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute a bias-corrected accelerated bootstrap interval

Stata 

bootstrap mean=r(mean), reps(499) bca: summarize y

R boot 

{ boot_fit <- boot::boot(data,function(d,i) mean(d$y[i]),R=499); boot::boot.ci(boot_fit,type="bca") }

Fixed workflow. Random streams and resampling defaults differ across software; a fixed R seed makes this workflow reproducible.

bsample

Draw a nonparametric row-bootstrap sample

Stata 

bsample

R base 

data[sample.int(nrow(data),nrow(data),replace=TRUE),,drop=FALSE]

Fixed workflow. Random streams and resampling defaults differ across software; a fixed R seed makes this workflow reproducible.

Stata reference · R reference

Draw a stratified row-bootstrap sample

Stata 

bsample, strata(g)

R base 

do.call(rbind,lapply(split(data,data$g),function(d) d[sample.int(nrow(d),nrow(d),replace=TRUE),,drop=FALSE]))

Fixed workflow. Random streams and resampling defaults differ across software; a fixed R seed makes this workflow reproducible.

jackknife

Jackknife a regression slope

Stata 

jackknife _b[x]: regress y x

R stats 

{ n <- nrow(data); deleted <- vapply(seq_len(n),function(i) unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(y~x,data=data[-i,]))["x"]),numeric(1)); c(estimate=unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(y~x,data=data))["x"]),se=sqrt((n-1)/n*sum((deleted-mean(deleted))^2))) }

Fixed workflow. The delete-one jackknife is deterministic; its variance uses (n-1)/n times the squared deviations of the replicate estimates.

Stata reference · R reference

Jackknife the sample mean

Stata 

jackknife mean=r(mean), rclass: summarize y

R stats 

{ n <- nrow(data); deleted <- vapply(seq_len(n),function(i) mean(data$y[-i]),numeric(1)); c(estimate=mean(data$y),se=sqrt((n-1)/n*sum((deleted-mean(deleted))^2))) }

Fixed workflow. The delete-one jackknife is deterministic; its variance uses (n-1)/n times the squared deviations of the replicate estimates.

Fixed workflow. The delete-one jackknife is deterministic; its variance uses (n-1)/n times the squared deviations of the replicate estimates.

simulate

Simulate the sampling distribution of a normal sample mean

Stata 

program define mymean, rclass
    preserve
    clear
    set obs 40
    generate y = rnormal(2,1)
    summarize y
    local estimate = r(mean)
    restore
    return scalar mean = `estimate'
end
simulate mean=r(mean), reps(199): mymean

R stats 

replicate(199,mean(stats::rnorm(40,mean=2,sd=1)))

Fixed workflow. mymean is a user-defined Stata program drawing 40 normal(2,1) observations and returning their mean; this is a fixed workflow.
